{{Short description|American mathematical biologist}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=April 2021}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=April 2021}}
'''Denise Ellen Kirschner''' is an American [[mathematical biology|mathematical biologist]] and [[immunology|immunologist]] whose research topics include [[granuloma]]s, [[HIV]], [[tuberculosis]], and the mechanisms by which disease pathogens interact with and persist in their hosts. She is a professor of microbiology and immunology at the [[University of Michigan]],{{r|umich}} co-editor-in-chief of the ''[[Journal of Theoretical Biology]]'',{{r|jtb}} and former president of the [[Society for Mathematical Biology]].

==Education and career==
Kirschner graduated from [[Tulane University]] in 1985, and completed her Ph.D. there in 1991.{{r|pro}} Her dissertation, ''Mathematical Modeling of the AIDS Virus in Epidemiology and Immunology'', was jointly supervised by [[Jerome Goldstein]] and [[James (Mac) Hyman]].{{r|mg}}

After postdoctoral research at [[Vanderbilt University]], she was an assistant professor at [[Texas A&M University]] from 1994 to 1997 before moving to the University of Michigan.{{r|pro}}

She was president of the Society for Mathematical Biology from 2017 to 2019.{{r|smb}} She is a speaker of the IBS Biomedical Mathematics Group.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Denise Kirschner |url=https://www.ibs.re.kr/bimag/speaker/denise-kirschner/ |access-date=2024-07-27 |website=Biomedical Mathematics Group |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Kirschner was listed as one of the inaugural Fellows of the Society for Mathematical Biology, in the class of 2017.{{r|smb}} She was named a [[SIAM Fellow]] in the 2021 class of fellows, "for contributions to modeling pathogen-host interactions and host immune response in infectious diseases and training in mathematical biology/immunology".{{r|sf}} In 2025, Kirschner was elected a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Microbiology]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=65 Fellows Elected Into the American Academy of Microbiology |url=https://asm.org/Press-Releases/2025/February/65-Fellows-Elected-Into-the-American-Academy-of-Mi |access-date=2025-03-06 |website=ASM.org |language=en}}</ref>
